Q: Delete line if substitution would leave it empty A:

Does what is asked, with -p

perl -wpe's/\s*\n*// if s/foo//g and not /\S/'  < input.txt

(I added an extra empty line to code for readability)

If any foo were indeed removed and no non-space characters is left then also remove all space and linefeeds -- so the remaining blank-or-space-only line won't show, in that case. (The original blank lines are unaffected as no foo was removed from them so the condition fails)

Or, in a more explicit form with -n to show what it's doing

perl -wne'print if not /\S/; $v = s/foo//gr and $v =~ /\S/ and print $v'

(I added an extra blank line for readability)

Print a line if it has no non-space characters (is blank). Then remove all foo and check whether there is any non-space character left so to print. (This fails for empty lines, printed initially.)

Tweak it if you want it to look nicer, it's possible

Here is one alternative

perl -wne'print if not /\S/ or (s/foo//gr and /\S/)'

Can actually remove parenthesis if you wish but then the logic of that conditional gets tricky

Q: ESP32 Bluetooth webserver A:

The protocols for BlueTooth (BT), web servers, and WiFi hotspots are all completely different. WiFi hotspots act as routers or hubs that push data through them, but don't actually serve web pages. BT is basically two endpoints that talk directly to each other, but when it's used as a WiFi hotspot, the software on the computer/mobile device sends that information over it's internet access to act like a regular WiFi router. That's not inherent to BT devices. To use BT to access your ESP32 application server, you need to write software, or use a 3rd party library, to translate the information received over the BT protocol into a protocol that accesses the web server, then translates the response back into the BT protocol. I'd assume someone has already done that so you can use a library, but I haven't researched that for myself.

Q: How NSwag handles anyOf A:

There is no option to solve it. NSwag doesn't support anyOf for nullables (as of v14.7.1).

You can track the issue (thanks @kemsky): https://github.com/RicoSuter/NSwag/issues/5215

A simple workaround is to replace anyOf with oneOf.
